newsitem.title: PERU: Miners who dug Peru rescue tunnels missing.
newsitem.headline: Miners who dug Peru rescue tunnels missing.

text.p: Two dozen state miners, who built the tunnels from which Peru launched its spectacular military operation against Marxist hostage-takers, have "disappeared" since the raid, according to relatives and media reports.
Dubbing the miners the "secret heroes" of the April 22 crushing of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement's (MRTA) siege, local television station Panamericana has led the campaign to find them.
The station has reported in recent days that the miners were obliged to leave their homes in the central Andes in January to take part in a secret "civic action."

Since then, their families, who were originally told the men had gone to the highland city of Puno, have had minimal contact with the men. Some letters were exchanged and four wives made a two-hour visit, supervised by officials, to their husbands, according to media interviews with the families.
They allege Peruvian authorities are hiding the miners illegally after they were pressured into three months' of work digging under the besieged Japanese ambassador's home.

Leading local human rights group Aprodeh has called on officials to reveal the miners' whereabouts, but warned they might have consented to hide to avoid reprisals from the MRTA or unwanted media attention.

"We believe that (the disappearance) has occurred, but it is not clear if there was a crime," said Aprodeh deputy director Miguel Jugo. "In the worst case, this is a question of detention, kidnap and -- if they do not turn up -- the 'disappearance' of people."
Peruvian authorities have so far kept quiet on the subject, declining to confirm the whereabouts on the miners or on reports that they are missing.
Adding to families' anxiety, local media have reported that two of the miners died during the building of the tunnel.
